details:
Project Najm is an advanced, climate-resilient agricultural decision-support platform designed to protect local farming against extreme weather and water scarcity. It functions by fusing real-time and historical NASA satellite data—specifically SMAP for surface and root-zone soil moisture, MODIS/Landsat for monitoring crop health and vegetation indices (NDVI), and NEX-GDDP for future climate and temperature projections.

Najm creates a digital twin of local fields, running AI-driven climate-shift simulations to recommend optimal, adaptive crop rotation and smart irrigation strategies. The anticipated impact includes reducing irrigation waste by up to 35%, preventing soil degradation, protecting farmers from crop failure, and boosting regional food security.

The project leverages robust data integration algorithms, climate simulation modeling, and structured digital workflows to translate complex satellite telemetry into clear, actionable, and practical plans for everyday farmers.
